analyst_view.overall: Early view: Sporting are 3rd and host Marítimo on Friday 4 December, five days after the trip to Porto and four days before a Champions League game at Roma, so Paulo Fonseca may rotate. Marítimo are 15th, have conceded 21 in 10, but kept the score to 2-1 in the League Cup at Alvalade with a back three that van der Gaag wants to keep. The site gives Sporting a huge edge, which looks fair, but the margin may be smaller than the 4.2 goals suggests.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.2 goals, which looks too high. Marítimo's back three held Sporting to a 2-1 in the League Cup at Alvalade, and Fonseca's first league game was only a 1-0 win over Moreirense. With rotation likely between Porto and Roma, I expect a Sporting win by two rather than a rout.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners, 6.1 for Sporting. I lean higher: a back five sitting deep at Alvalade usually concedes plenty of corners, as Sporting work the ball wide and cross. Marítimo will add very few of their own.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. Marítimo will defend for long spells, which brings fouls, but one-sided games at Alvalade are rarely bad-tempered. I keep to the site's figure.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.0 shots, 20.2 for Sporting. Against a deep back three Sporting should have plenty of attempts even with a rotated side, and Marítimo will try a few from distance. The volume looks about right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target. A packed defence blocks a lot of attempts before they reach the goalkeeper, and a rotated Sporting side may be less sharp. I lean slightly lower.
